name: Pipeliners - AI Answer Batch 1 2026-09-29
body:
> Report · Pipeliners · 2026-09-29

# Summary
Work folder for "AI-answer readiness, batch 1" (Sep 29, 2026): six ad-free blog posts got only the pieces they were missing for AI answers (answer-first blocks and a short FAQ with matching schema). No write notes exist in the folder; this summary comes from the script headers and the after/summary.json file.

# Key findings
- Posts: 13740 /what-causes-pinhole-leaks-in-copper-pipes/, 13684 /cipp-vs-traditional-sewer-line-replacement-pros-and-cons/, 13736 /14-warning-signs-your-sewer-pipes-may-be-leaking/, 14947 /is-trenchless-sewer-repair-more-expensive-than-digging/, 13720 /should-i-diy-pipe-repair/, 14832 /reline-vs-replace-best-options-for-drain-and-sewer-pipes/.
- Each got 3 to 4 FAQ questions (for example on pinhole leaks: can an epoxy coating stop them, how to find one you cannot see, repipe or coat, is one pinhole a sign of more).
- Claims allowed: client service pages (20 to 30% savings vs digging, UV LED liners with a 50-year life expectancy, ePIPE process and NSF/ANSI 61), the site's own cost post (curing times, job length), and Kim-confirmed claims (24/7, leak-locating equipment). No new prices, warranties or unverified claims.
- Apply script was a guarded dry run unless explicitly enabled, and required live content to equal the saved "before" copy. A follow-up script converted CRLF to LF in the six posts.

# Files in this folder (rollups only)
- `before/` and `after/` content HTML and FAQ JSON per post, `after/summary.json`, `batch1-preview.html`, `live/` desktop and mobile HTML and headers. PHP and Python scripts not summarized.
